narrative:
The model estimates a 57% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors about your profile.

Your relatively short overall work experience of just 1-5 years was the strongest influence pulling the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expected to stay, only about half had similarly limited experience, while many had 6 or more years. This limited background makes the system less confident you'll remain long-term.

Two other factors pushed in the opposite direction, slightly encouraging the model to predict you would stay. Having received other job offers while working here signals that you are valued in the market, which the model sees as a reason you might choose to remain. Similarly, having spent 1-5 years already in this organization (rather than being brand new) also mildly supported a prediction of staying, though not enough to outweigh your shorter total career experience.

The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you directly and exploring ways to build your long-term commitment, such as targeted development opportunities. You may want to reflect on whether this role aligns with your aspirations and what would make you want to grow here.
